children.name: Permissions Figma has four different levels of access: Viewers, Editors, Admins, and Owners. When you share a file, you can specify which level of access you’d like for each person you’re sharing the file with.
children.characters:
Permissions
Figma has four different levels of access: Viewers, Editors, Admins, and Owners. When you share a file, you can specify which level of access you’d like for each person you’re sharing the file with.

children.name: Share an individual Frame In addition to sharing a file, you can link to a selected frame on the canvas so it’ll be zoomed and in focus when your collaborators open the file.
children.characters:
Share an individual Frame

children.name: Sharing your files in Figma is simple. Open the share dialog to set specific permissions or enable link access. With link access enabled, sharing a file is as easy as sharing its URL.
children.characters: Sharing your files in Figma is simple. Open the share dialog to set specific permissions or enable link access. With link access enabled, sharing a file is as easy as sharing its URL.

children.name: Adding comments To add, view, and respond to comments, you’ll need to enter Comment mode by clicking on the Comment icon in the toolbar. Then, click on anywhere on the canvas to add your comment. You’re also able to @mention someone on your team so s/he receives an email notification.
children.characters:
Adding comments
To add, view, and respond to comments, you’ll need to enter Comment mode by clicking on the Comment icon in the toolbar. Then, click on anywhere on the canvas to add your comment.
You’re also able to @mention someone on your team so s/he receives an email notification.

children.name: Notifications The properties panel has additional options to show resolved comments and whether or not to receive email notifications for new comments and replies.
children.characters:
Notifications
The properties panel has additional options to show resolved comments and whether or not to receive email notifications for new comments and replies.

children.name: Comments add another layer of collaboration in Figma. You can add comments anywhere on the canvas. Comments can be added to both the design file as well as prototypes.
children.characters: Comments add another layer of collaboration in Figma. You can add comments anywhere on the canvas. Comments can be added to both the design file as well as prototypes.

children.name: Select the Comment tool and add a comment to the Frame below.
children.characters: Select the Comment tool            and add a comment to the Frame below.

children.name: Make your selections First choose which elements of your design you’d like to export. You can export single layers or objects, multiple layers or objects, individual group or frame, multiple groups and frames, and even your entire canvas.
children.characters:
Make your selections
First choose which elements of your design you’d like to export. You can export single layers or objects, multiple layers or objects, individual group or frame, multiple groups and frames, and even your entire canvas.

children.name: Apply export settings You can define exactly how you would like your objects, layers, or frames to be exported, using the Export settings in the Properties panel. Figma supports exporting in PNG, JPG, SVG, and PDF formats as well as in a variety of screen density multipliers and appending suffixes to filenames.
children.characters:
Apply export settings
You can define exactly how you would like your objects, layers, or frames to be exported, using the Export settings in the Properties panel.
Figma supports exporting in PNG, JPG, SVG, and PDF formats as well as in a variety of screen density multipliers and appending suffixes to filenames.

children.name: Exporting your selection Once export settings have been applied to a selection, that selection will be recorded in the Export list. You can then export your selections with a single action in the future. Search for “export” in the menu.
children.characters:
Exporting your selection
Once export settings have been applied to a selection, that selection will be recorded in the Export list. You can then export your selections with a single action in the future. Search for “export” in the menu.

children.name: Figma supports exporting in PNG, JPG, SVG, and PDF formats. When using Figma in the browser, exports will be automatically saved to your default download folder. Try exporting using the Figma desktop app to choose where to save.
children.characters: Figma supports exporting in PNG, JPG, SVG, and PDF formats. When using Figma in the browser, exports will be automatically saved to your default download folder. Try exporting using the Figma desktop app to choose where to save.

children.name: How Smart Selection works Smart Selection works automatically on any selection or group of 3 or more items with equal, uniform spacing. With items selected, you can adjust spacing, position, and size of all these items at once by dragging the pink handles.
children.characters:
How Smart Selection works
Smart Selection works automatically on any selection or group of 3 or more items with equal, uniform spacing. With items selected, you can adjust spacing, position, and size of all these items at once by dragging the pink handles.

children.name: Smart Selection allows you to quickly adjust spacing between objects, create an uniform grid by a selection of objects, and rearrange objects within a grid layout. Think of grid layouts for inbox interfaces, news feeds, and photo galleries.
children.characters: Smart Selection allows you to quickly adjust spacing between objects, create an uniform grid by a selection of objects, and rearrange objects within a grid layout. Think of grid layouts for inbox interfaces, news feeds, and photo galleries.

children.name: See how Smart Selection works with the two examples below.
children.characters: See how Smart Selection works with the two examples below.

children.name: How to create Color Styles Select the object you’d like to create a Style for and in the Properties panel, click the Styles icon next to the property you would like to save. Click the “+” icon and you’ll be prompted to give your Style a name.
children.characters:
How to create Color Styles
Select the object you’d like to create a Style for and in the Properties panel, click the Styles icon next to the property you would like to save. Click the “+” icon and you’ll be prompted to give your Style a name.

children.name: How to create Text Styles Select the text you’d like to create a Style for and click the Style icon within the text properties in the Properties panel. Click the “+” icon and you’ll be prompted to give your Style a name.
children.characters:
How to create Text Styles
Select the text you’d like to create a Style for and click the Style icon within the text properties in the Properties panel. Click the “+” icon and you’ll be prompted to give your Style a name.

children.name: The Styles feature allows you to define a set of properties like color, font, and effects of an object, that can be reused across your team's designs. Whenever you make a change to a Style’s properties, any objects using that Style will be instantly updated.
children.characters: The Styles feature allows you to define a set of properties like color, font, and effects of an object, that can be reused across your team's designs. Whenever you make a change to a Style’s properties, any objects using that Style will be instantly updated.

children.name: 2. Applying Styles Notice how the 2nd and 3rd chat bubbles have different text and color? Try applying your newly created Text and Color Styles to them so they’re all consistent.

children.name: Components enable you to reuse existing parts of your design, saving time on otherwise repetitive and tedious work. Components create new instances rather than copies, allowing you to override properties directly on the canvas.
children.characters: Components enable you to reuse existing parts of your design, saving time on otherwise repetitive and tedious work. Components create new instances rather than copies, allowing you to override properties directly on the canvas.

children.name: Creating components Select the layers you want to include in your Main Component and either use the Create Component button at the top or use the right-click menu to create a new component.
children.characters:
Creating components
Select the layers you want to include in your Main Component and either use the Create Component button at the top or use the right-click menu to create a new component.

children.name: There are two aspects to a Component: 1. The Main Component, which defines the properties of the Component. 2. The Instance, which is a copy of the Component that you can reuse in your designs. Instances are linked to the Main Component, so any changes you make to the Main Component will be applied to the Instance.
children.characters:
There are two aspects to a Component:
1. The Main Component, which defines the properties of the Component.
2. The Instance, which is a copy of the Component that you can reuse in your designs.
Instances are linked to the Main Component, so any changes you make to the Main Component will be applied to the Instance.

children.name: Asset panel The Asset panel will house all of your components. Just drag and drop them onto the canvas to create a new instance.
children.characters:
Asset panel
The Asset panel will house all of your components. Just drag and drop them onto the canvas to create a new instance.

children.name: 1. Create a Component Select the grouped object below and make it a Component by using the Create Component icon above or via the right-click menu and selecting Create Component. This is now the Main Component that you can duplicate to create new instances of it.
children.characters:
1. Create a Component

children.name: 2. Duplicate the Main Component Open the Assets panel at the top-left and drag an instance of your new Component into the “Chats” frame below. Try adding a few more instances and then override the image fill and text to create the mockup you see on the right.

children.name: Ignoring constraints You may want to resize an object, without applying any constraints. To ignore an object’s constraints, hold down the modifier key and resize the object.
children.characters:
Ignoring constraints
You may want to resize an object, without applying any constraints. To ignore an object’s constraints, hold down the modifier key and resize the object.

children.name: Constraints allow you to fix elements of your design to different sides of their parent Frame. This lets you build fluid layouts to support multiple device sizes and breakpoints within the same group.
children.characters: Constraints allow you to fix elements of your design to different sides of their parent Frame. This lets you build fluid layouts to support multiple device sizes and breakpoints within the same group.

children.characters: Horizontal and vertical constraints can be set independently

children.name: Right and Bottom maintains the object’s position, relative to the right-side and bottom of the frame.
children.characters: Right and Bottom maintains the object’s position, relative to the right-side and bottom of the frame.

children.name: Center maintains the object’s position, relative to the horizontal and vertical center of the frame.
children.characters: Center maintains the object’s position, relative to the horizontal and vertical center of the frame.

children.name: Scale maintains the object’s size and position as a percentage of the Frame’s dimensions.

children.name: 2. Resize this Frame’s width The input fields as well as button have left & right constraints applied to them making them expand to fill the viewport as the frame’s width is resized.

children.name: Frames in Figma are what you may think of as artboards in other design tools. Frames are a foundational element for your designs that act as a top-level container for most things you create in Figma. There are a few different ways to create frames in Figma:
children.characters: Frames in Figma are what you may think of as artboards in other design tools. Frames are a foundational element for your designs that act as a top-level container for most things you create in Figma. There are a few different ways to create frames in Figma:

children.name: Custom sizes Create custom sized frames by selecting the frame tool and click and drag your cursor to the desired size.
children.characters:
Custom sizes
Create custom sized frames by selecting the frame tool and click and drag your cursor to the desired size.

children.name: Preset sizes Create frames with preset sizes, e.g. iPhone X, by selecting the preset in the Properties panel on the right-hand side.
children.characters:
Preset sizes

children.name: Existing elements Create frames from existing elements on the canvas by right-clicking and selecting Frame Selection.
children.characters:
Existing elements
